topic: Support-aware and uncertainty-aware conservatism in offline and offline-to-online RL (novelty check for support-aware fine-tuning)

papers.title: Stabilizing Off-Policy Q-Learning via Bootstrapping Error Reduction
papers.authors: Aviral Kumar, Justin Fu, George Tucker, Sergey Levine
papers.summary: BEAR shows that Bellman backups query out-of-distribution actions, which compounds bootstrapping error. It constrains the actor to the support of the behavior policy with a sampled MMD constraint rather than matching its density, and backs up with an ensemble of Q-functions.
papers.relevance: This is the canonical support-matching (not distribution-matching) argument. Our option (c) is a per-action, discrete version of the same idea. In discrete recommendation, support can be read directly from pi_beta(a|s) instead of being estimated through MMD on samples. We cite it as motivation and do not claim the support-versus-density distinction as ours.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the title, authors and 2019 date. Its comments field says 'Accepted at NeurIPS 2019'.

papers.title: Benchmarking Batch Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
papers.authors: Scott Fujimoto, Edoardo Conti, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Joelle Pineau
papers.summary: This paper adapts BCQ to discrete actions. It trains a BC model G(a|s) and restricts the argmax in Q-learning to actions with G(a|s)/max_a' G(a'|s) > tau, which is a hard, per-state, relative-support mask. It benchmarks batch RL algorithms on Atari. The original continuous BCQ is Fujimoto, Meger and Precup, ICML 2019 (arXiv 1812.02900).
papers.relevance: This is the most direct prior art for option (c) in discrete actions: a support threshold on an estimated behavior policy. Annealing or relaxing tau during online fine-tuning is an obvious extension, not a new method. It is a mandatory baseline, and the tau sweep also serves as a support-masking ablation.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors, the date (Oct 2019) and 'Deep RL Workshop NeurIPS 2019'. Section 4 of the PDF (Eq. 17-18) confirms the relative threshold G(a|s)/max G(a^|s) > tau in both the policy and the target.

papers.title: Supported Policy Optimization for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Jialong Wu, Haixu Wu, Zihan Qiu, Jianmin Wang, Mingsheng Long
papers.summary: SPOT adds a density-based support regularizer (a VAE ELBO estimate of log pi_beta(a|s)) to the actor objective of an off-policy algorithm (TD3). For online fine-tuning (Sec. 5.3 and App. C.3), the regularization weight lambda is decayed linearly and the decay stops at 20% of the initial value at step 0.8M. The VAE stays fixed during fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: SPOT is the closest prior work for option (a) as a policy-side support penalty, and its fine-tuning protocol is a global, time-only schedule. Varying lambda per state-action by support, or updating the support model online, goes beyond SPOT. A 'global lambda decay' baseline in the SPOT style is needed to show that per-sample modulation matters. In discrete actions, log pi_beta is exact when the behavior policy is known.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page lists no venue. NeurIPS 2022 is confirmed by the NeurIPS proceedings and poster page (neurips.cc/virtual/2022/poster/55125). The PDF text checks out: Sec. 5.3 says 'we fix the VAE during online fine-tuning', and App. C.3 says 'stop decay when lambda reaches the 20% of its initial value at the 0.8M-th step'.

papers.title: Supported Value Regularization for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Yixiu Mao, Hongchang Zhang, Chen Chen, Yi Xu, Xiangyang Ji
papers.summary: SVR penalizes Q-values over the whole OOD action region (actions outside the behavior support) and keeps standard Bellman updates for in-distribution actions. It computes the summed OOD Q-values using the bias of importance sampling with the behavior policy. In the tabular case the operator is a contraction, and policy iteration converges to the optimal support-constrained policy.
papers.relevance: SVR is the value-side analogue of support-aware conservatism and is very close to 'per state-action support-weighted CQL' in option (a). In discrete actions, the OOD set {a: pi_beta(a|s)=0} can be enumerated exactly, so an SVR-style discrete penalty is a natural baseline or variant. SVR is offline-only and is evaluated on continuous D4RL, so the remaining difference is the fine-tuning regime and the discrete recommendation setting.
papers.correction_note: The NeurIPS 2023 poster page confirms the title, authors and abstract. A web search found no arXiv version, which is fine; the only same-author arXiv hit is a different paper (STR, 2311.08935). The proceedings PDF is at papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/7fa46657df480226112d5be3faf096c4-Paper-Conference.pdf.

papers.title: Mildly Conservative Q-Learning for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Jiafei Lyu, Xiaoteng Ma, Xiu Li, Zongqing Lu
papers.summary: MCQ trains OOD actions toward pseudo Q-targets, computed from the maximum Q over actions sampled from an estimated behavior policy, instead of pushing them down without limit. It argues the resulting policy is no worse than the behavior policy, and it shows better offline-to-online transfer than CQL.
papers.relevance: MCQ shows that mild, support-referenced conservatism helps fine-tuning. In discrete actions, its pseudo-target (max Q over supported actions) is cheap to compute exactly. It is a candidate 'mild conservatism' comparator, so our claim cannot be that 'less pessimism on OOD actions helps O2O'.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the title, authors and the NeurIPS 2022 comment, and the abstract mentions offline-to-online transfer.

papers.title: Uncertainty Weighted Actor-Critic for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Yue Wu, Shuangfei Zhai, Nitish Srivastava, Joshua Susskind, Jian Zhang, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Hanlin Goh
papers.summary: UWAC estimates epistemic uncertainty of Q(s,a) with MC dropout and down-weights the critic and actor losses of high-uncertainty (likely OOD) state-action pairs by an inverse-variance weight.
papers.relevance: This is prior art for per-sample loss reweighting by uncertainty, which is the mechanical core of options (a) and (b). It is offline-only. Our weighting uses support or density, or ensemble disagreement, during fine-tuning, but the reweighting device itself is not novel.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors, the 2021 date and 'To appear in ICML 2021', and the abstract confirms dropout-based uncertainty.

papers.title: Pessimistic Bootstrapping for Uncertainty-Driven Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Chenjia Bai, Lingxiao Wang, Zhuoran Yang, Zhihong Deng, Animesh Garg, Peng Liu, Zhaoran Wang
papers.summary: PBRL penalizes Bellman targets by the standard deviation of a bootstrapped Q-ensemble (K=10) and adds OOD action sampling with its own pessimistic target. The OOD penalty weight beta_ood is decayed during offline training: linearly over the first 50K steps, then exponentially. It gives a provable uncertainty quantifier in linear MDPs, where ensemble disagreement corresponds to the elliptical LCB term sqrt(phi^T Lambda^-1 phi), which behaves like an inverse count. The paper is offline-only and has no offline-to-online fine-tuning experiment.
papers.relevance: PBRL is the closest offline prior work for option (b). Its linear-MDP result that ensemble std approximates inverse coverage is exactly the link between (a) and (b) that our simulator can test empirically, because the true support is known.
papers.correction_note: The title, authors, year and venue (ICLR 2022) are correct. The original summary said 'The paper also includes an offline-to-online experiment with a decaying penalty', which is not supported. A full-text search of the PDF found no fine-tuning or offline-to-online experiment. The only decay is of beta_ood during offline training (Sec. 3 and the hyperparameter table: 5.0 to 0.2, linear then exponential).

papers.title: Uncertainty-Based Offline Reinforcement Learning with Diversified Q-Ensemble
papers.authors: Gaon An, Seungyong Moon, Jang-Hyun Kim, Hyun Oh Song
papers.summary: SAC-N and EDAC take the minimum over a large Q-ensemble (clipped Q-learning) as an implicit uncertainty penalty on OOD actions. EDAC adds a gradient-diversity term so far fewer ensemble members are needed.
papers.relevance: This is a baseline for ensemble-based conservatism with no explicit behavior model. In discrete recommendation with thousands of items, min-over-ensemble is cheap. It is a natural 'implicit uncertainty' arm to compare against explicit pi_beta support.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors, the 2021 date and 'To appear at NeurIPS 2021'.

papers.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning as Anti-Exploration
papers.authors: Shideh Rezaeifar, Robert Dadashi, Nino Vieillard, Leonard Hussenot, Olivier Bachem, Olivier Pietquin, Matthieu Geist
papers.venue: AAAI 2022 (Proc. AAAI vol. 36, no. 7, pp. 8106-8114; arXiv 2106.06431, June 2021)
papers.summary: This paper subtracts an exploration-style bonus (VAE prediction error on (s,a)) from the reward, so the agent avoids poorly supported actions. It frames offline RL as the reverse of novelty-seeking exploration.
papers.relevance: The framing is useful: a support-aware penalty offline becomes an exploration bonus online, and flipping its sign or annealing it during fine-tuning is the natural O2O extension. In discrete recommendation, a count or pi_beta-based bonus replaces the VAE.
papers.correction_note: The venue was listed as unconfirmed. AAAI 2022 is now confirmed on the AAAI OJS page (ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/20783, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v36i7.20783), which also matches the authors. The year is set to 2022 for the publication; the arXiv preprint dates from 2021.

papers.title: Anti-Exploration by Random Network Distillation
papers.authors: Alexander Nikulin, Vladislav Kurenkov, Denis Tarasov, Sergey Kolesnikov
papers.summary: SAC-RND uses RND prediction error, with FiLM conditioning of the action on the state, as an ensemble-free anti-exploration penalty in SAC. It matches ensemble methods on D4RL.
papers.relevance: RND on (s, item embedding) is a cheap learned pseudo-count for discrete items. It is a third way to estimate support, alongside pi_beta-BC and ensemble disagreement, and fits the 'which support signal' ablation.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors, the 2023 date and ICML 2023 (poster).

papers.title: Model-based Offline Reinforcement Learning with Count-based Conservatism
papers.authors: Byeongchan Kim, Min-hwan Oh
papers.summary: Count-MORL bounds model error by a quantity inversely proportional to state-action visit counts, estimated with hash codes. It penalizes model-based rollouts accordingly and gives near-optimality guarantees.
papers.relevance: This is the closest prior work for explicit count-based conservatism. In our discrete setting, item-level and (state-cluster, item) counts are exact, so count-weighted penalties are an easy, honest baseline. It is offline and model-based only.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and 'Accepted at ICML 2023'.

papers.title: MOPO: Model-based Offline Policy Optimization
papers.authors: Tianhe Yu, Garrett Thomas, Lantao Yu, Stefano Ermon, James Zou, Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn, Tengyu Ma
papers.summary: MOPO penalizes rewards in model rollouts by the learned dynamics model's uncertainty. In practice the penalty is the maximum, over ensemble members, of the norm of each Gaussian model's predicted std. This maximizes a lower bound on true return. A companion paper is MOReL (Kidambi et al., NeurIPS 2020, arXiv 2005.05951), which builds a pessimistic MDP with an absorbing halt state in uncertain regions.
papers.relevance: Model-uncertainty penalties are what recommender offline RL (e.g., DORL on KuaiRec) uses. If we use a learned user model, a MOPO-style penalty is the standard baseline. Our method is model-free, and its support signal comes from the logging policy rather than model error.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and NeurIPS 2020. One wording fix: the penalty is the max over members of each model's predicted std, not the std across the ensemble.

papers.title: Confidence-Conditioned Value Functions for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Joey Hong, Aviral Kumar, Sergey Levine
papers.summary: This paper learns Q(s,a,delta) conditioned on a confidence level delta, which sets how conservative the estimate is. At evaluation time a confidence-adaptive policy picks delta from the history of observations using a Bellman-consistency criterion (inspired by Ghosh et al. 2022), not from observed returns. Experiments are on discrete actions: an 8x8 gridworld, offline Atari (17 games), and online fine-tuning on 5 Atari games (Sec. 7.3).
papers.relevance: It is close to the 'adapt conservatism online' idea and is in discrete actions. It already includes an offline-to-online Atari experiment. It adapts one confidence level per history (shared across actions) through Bellman consistency, not per action by offline support. A confidence-conditioned critic could replace our hand-designed support weighting. This must be acknowledged in any claim about adaptive conservatism.
papers.correction_note: The title, authors and venue are correct (ICLR 2023, per the arXiv comments). The method detail is corrected: delta is chosen from the observation history via Bellman consistency (Sec. 4.2), not 'from returns observed online'. The paper also has an online fine-tuning experiment on Atari (Sec. 7.3), which the original entry left out.

papers.title: ACL-QL: Adaptive Conservative Level in Q-Learning for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Kun Wu, Yinuo Zhao, Zhiyuan Xu, Zhengping Che, Chengxiang Yin, Chi Harold Liu, Feiferi Feng, Jian Tang
papers.summary: ACL-QL replaces CQL's single alpha with two learnable weight functions that set a per-state-action conservative level. It trains them with a monotonicity loss so that better transitions are penalized less.
papers.relevance: This is direct prior art for 'per state-action CQL weights'. The difference is that ACL-QL learns the weights from transition quality offline, whereas ours would be tied to an interpretable support signal and applied during fine-tuning. It means we cannot claim per-(s,a) adaptive alpha as new.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors as listed (including 'Feiferi Feng') and 'published in IEEE TNNLS (2024)', DOI 10.1109/TNNLS.2024.3497667.

papers.title: Strategically Conservative Q-Learning
papers.authors: Yutaka Shimizu, Joey Hong, Sergey Levine, Masayoshi Tomizuka
papers.summary: SCQ separates OOD actions that are easy to estimate (interpolation) from hard ones (extrapolation) and penalizes only the latter. It is conservative but less pessimistic than CQL.
papers.relevance: This is another state-action-selective conservatism method. It motivates an ablation: in item-embedding space, a low-support item may sit near well-supported items, so raw support counts can over-penalize it. Comparing count-based support against embedding-aware support (ensemble or RND) addresses this.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and the June 2024 date. Neither the arXiv page nor a web search shows a venue, so it is treated as a preprint.

papers.title: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning via Balanced Replay and Pessimistic Q-Ensemble
papers.authors: Seunghyun Lee, Younggyo Seo, Kimin Lee, Pieter Abbeel, Jinwoo Shin
papers.summary: This work fine-tunes CQL-pretrained agents with (i) balanced replay, which prioritizes near-on-policy samples from offline and online data using a learned density ratio, and (ii) a pessimistic Q-ensemble to avoid overoptimism on unfamiliar actions early in fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: It is the closest prior work for option (d), plus ensemble pessimism during fine-tuning (option b). Density-ratio-prioritized mixing of offline and online data already exists, so a 'support-aware replay mix' alone is not novel. It is a key baseline.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and CoRL 2021.

papers.title: ENOTO: Improving Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning with Q-Ensembles
papers.authors: Kai Zhao, Jianye Hao, Yi Ma, Jinyi Liu, Yan Zheng, Zhaopeng Meng
papers.venue: IJCAI 2024 (pp. 5563-5571; arXiv 2306.06871, first posted June 2023 under the title 'Ensemble-based Offline-to-Online (E2O) RL')
papers.summary: ENOTO pretrains offline with a large Q-ensemble and a MinQ (min over all members) target. At the start of online fine-tuning it switches once to a WeightedMinPair target (the expectation of pairwise-min targets over all N-choose-2 pairs), which loosens pessimism. It also adds SUNRISE-style ensemble-based exploration and weighted backups. The relaxation is a single switch, not a progressive schedule.
papers.relevance: This is the closest prior work for option (b) during fine-tuning: ensemble-based pessimism that is relaxed when fine-tuning starts. Making the relaxation gradual, or per-action by disagreement or support, is an incremental step beyond ENOTO, and ENOTO is a required baseline if (b) is pursued.
papers.correction_note: The venue was listed as unconfirmed; IJCAI 2024 is now confirmed (ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/615, DOI 10.24963/ijcai.2024/615). The method description is also corrected. The original summary said ENOTO 'progressively relaxes the pessimistic ensemble target... moving from min-style to mean or weighted targets'. Per Algorithm 1 of arXiv v4, it switches once from MinQ to WeightedMinPair at the start of the online phase, and the paper describes no gradual annealing.

papers.title: A Simple Unified Uncertainty-Guided Framework for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning (SUNG)
papers.authors: Siyuan Guo, Yanchao Sun, Jifeng Hu, Sili Huang, Hechang Chen, Haiyin Piao, Lichao Sun, Yi Chang
papers.venue: arXiv 2306.07541; final version in IEEE Xplore (DOI 10.1109/TNNLS.2025.3633997, i.e., IEEE TNNLS 2025)
papers.summary: SUNG estimates state-action uncertainty with a VAE visitation-density model (ELBO). The VAE keeps being updated online (Alg. 1, line 19). During fine-tuning, the top p% of each minibatch by uncertainty is marked OOD with a binary identifier I(s,a), which the paper says 'can be performed by sampling from a categorical distribution'. Those samples get the offline-RL regularizer: TD3+BC (SPOT on AntMaze) or CQL. The rest get the standard online objective, and p=0 or p=100 recovers pure online or pure offline. Exploration uses bi-level action selection: the top-k candidates by Q (or by uncertainty), then softmax sampling on the other criterion. It also uses an offline-to-online replay buffer.
papers.relevance: This is the single closest prior work to our option (a): per-sample, density-gated conservatism during online fine-tuning. Our version would differ only in (i) discrete actions with exact or oracle pi_beta, (ii) soft weighting instead of a binary top-p% identifier, and (iii) the recommendation simulator. These are differences of instantiation and analysis, not of algorithmic idea. SUNG is evaluated only on continuous D4RL (MuJoCo and AntMaze).
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page and PDF text confirm the authors, the VAE density estimate, the top-p% identifier and the online VAE updates. One clarification: the arXiv comment says only that the final version is on IEEE Xplore and does not name the journal; TNNLS is inferred from the DOI. The top-p% selection may be stochastic (categorical sampling), but the identifier is binary.

papers.title: Train Once, Get a Family: State-Adaptive Balances for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Shenzhi Wang, Qisen Yang, Jiawei Gao, Matthieu Gaetan Lin, Hao Chen, Liwei Wu, Ning Jia, Shiji Song, Gao Huang
papers.summary: FamO2O trains a universal policy conditioned on a balance coefficient between improvement and constraint, plus a balance model that selects the coefficient per state. It is a plug-in for O2O algorithms (e.g., IQL, AWAC).
papers.relevance: This is prior art for state-adaptive constraint strength in O2O, relevant to options (a) and (c). FamO2O learns the balance per state from returns, while ours derives it per (state, action) from offline support. Its per-state balance is a natural baseline for the per-action support signal.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and 'NeurIPS 2023 (spotlight)'.

papers.title: Cal-QL: Calibrated Offline RL Pre-Training for Efficient Online Fine-Tuning
papers.authors: Mitsuhiko Nakamoto, Yuexiang Zhai, Anikait Singh, Max Sobol Mark, Yi Ma, Chelsea Finn, Aviral Kumar, Sergey Levine
papers.summary: Cal-QL modifies the CQL push-down so learned Q-values are lower-bounded by a reference (behavior) policy's value, which makes the critic calibrated. This avoids the early 'unlearning' dip when fine-tuning starts. It is a one-line change to CQL.
papers.relevance: It is the standard O2O-from-CQL baseline and explains the initial-dip phenomenon that our 'when does online help or hurt' question must measure. Discrete Cal-QL is easy to implement because the Monte Carlo returns of the behavior policy are known in the simulator.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and NeurIPS 2023.

papers.title: Efficient Online Reinforcement Learning with Offline Data (RLPD)
papers.authors: Philip J. Ball, Laura Smith, Ilya Kostrikov, Sergey Levine
papers.summary: RLPD shows that plain off-policy RL works with offline data given symmetric 50/50 offline/online batch sampling, LayerNorm in the critic (which bounds extrapolated Q-values), and a large critic ensemble (10 by default, with random-subset targets), at a high update-to-data ratio.
papers.relevance: This is the key replay-mixing baseline for option (d) and a strong 'no explicit conservatism' control. If RLPD-style LayerNorm plus symmetric sampling matches support-aware fine-tuning, the support signal is not what matters.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and ICML 2023. The PDF confirms 'the 10 member ensemble we use by default'. The paper's title has no '(RLPD)' suffix; that was added in the entry.

papers.title: Adaptive Policy Learning for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Han Zheng, Xufang Luo, Pengfei Wei, Xuan Song, Dongsheng Li, Jing Jiang
papers.summary: APL applies pessimistic updates to samples from the offline dataset and optimistic or greedy updates to online samples. It is instantiated in both value-based and policy-based methods.
papers.relevance: This is prior art for treating data sources differently by origin, a coarse binary version of support awareness. Our per-(s,a) support weighting generalizes origin-based gating, and APL-style binary gating is the natural ablation, analogous to DARE's critique.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and AAAI 2023.

papers.title: Adaptive Behavior Cloning Regularization for Stable Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Yi Zhao, Rinu Boney, Alexander Ilin, Juho Kannala, Joni Pajarinen
papers.summary: This method adapts the TD3+BC behavior-cloning weight during fine-tuning based on recent performance and training stability, and uses a randomized Q-ensemble for high update-to-data ratios.
papers.relevance: It is a global, performance-driven relaxation of the policy constraint, the 'time-only' counterpart of option (c). It serves as a baseline separating whether adaptivity over time or adaptivity over support drives any gain.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and the Oct 2022 date and lists no venue.

papers.title: Evaluation-Time Policy Switching for Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Natinael Solomon Neggatu, Jeremie Houssineau, Giovanni Montana
papers.summary: This method trains an off-policy RL agent with a critic ensemble and a separate BC agent. At each state it switches between them using epistemic uncertainty from the ensemble and aleatoric uncertainty from the dataset. The authors report it extends to offline-to-online fine-tuning without extra tuning.
papers.relevance: This is close to option (c) in its 'fall back to behavior on uncertain states' form, and it already covers O2O. A recommendation version would gate at the item level (fall back to the BC or behavior distribution for low-support items), which is a modest difference.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and the journal-ref 'Proc. of AAMAS 2025'.

papers.title: From Static Constraints to Dynamic Adaptation: Sample-Level Constraint Relaxation for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning (DARE)
papers.authors: Lipeng Zu, Yu Qian, Shayok Chakraborty, Xiaonan Zhang
papers.venue: arXiv preprint 2511.03828 (v1 Nov 2025, v3 May 2026; no venue listed)
papers.summary: DARE scores each sample by the L2 deviation of its action from a behavior model's reference action. The behavior model is an energy-guided diffusion model, or alternatively the online actor. A two-Gaussian Bayes posterior over that deviation decides balanced, hard exchanges of samples between the offline-constrained and online-unconstrained objectives. It is built on Cal-QL (DARE-C) and on IQL with PEX (DARE-I).
papers.relevance: This is a very recent (2025-26) instance of sample-level, behavior-consistency-driven relaxation during O2O, which is essentially option (a)/(d) in continuous control. It confirms the idea space is actively occupied, and it is the strongest reason to frame our work as a discrete-recommendation design study rather than a new algorithm.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and the version dates (v1 5 Nov 2025, v2 1 May 2026, v3 17 May 2026). The mechanism is confirmed from the arXiv HTML. The full title has no '(DARE)' suffix; that was added in the entry.

papers.title: Alleviating Matthew Effect of Offline Reinforcement Learning in Interactive Recommendation (DORL)
papers.authors: Chongming Gao, Kexin Huang, Jiawei Chen, Yuan Zhang, Biao Li, Peng Jiang, Shiqi Wang, Zhong Zhang, Xiangnan He
papers.summary: DORL is model-based offline RL for recommendation, with KuaiRec (fully observed matrix as ground truth, normalized watch time as reward) and KuaiRand-Pure as environments. It uses a MOPO-style penalty (max over K Gaussian reward models of the predicted variance) and adds an entropy term that relaxes pessimism where the logging policy has high entropy, which counters the Matthew effect of uniform conservatism.
papers.relevance: This is the most relevant recommendation prior work. It shows on KuaiRec that uniform conservatism over-concentrates on popular items, and it already modulates pessimism by a logging-policy statistic (entropy), though offline-only and model-based. It is a required baseline or point of comparison. Our setup should report item-popularity and coverage metrics, as DORL does.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and 'SIGIR 2023 Full Paper'. The PDF text confirms KuaiRec and KuaiRand-Pure, normalized viewing time as reward, and the uncertainty penalty P_U = max over K of the predicted sigma^2.

papers.title: Efficient Online Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning Need Not Retain Offline Data (WSRL)
papers.authors: Zhiyuan Zhou, Andy Peng, Qiyang Li, Sergey Levine, Aviral Kumar
papers.summary: WSRL shows that keeping offline data during fine-tuning mainly prevents a Q-divergence at the start of fine-tuning caused by distribution mismatch. A short warm-up of pretrained-policy rollouts recalibrates the critic, so offline data can be dropped and plain online RL used.
papers.relevance: This is a counterpoint for option (d). It suggests the offline/online mixing ratio matters mostly early in fine-tuning, so any support-aware mixing must be compared against a warm-up-only, no-retention baseline.
papers.correction_note: The arXiv page confirms the authors and the journal-ref ICLR 2025. The title has no '(WSRL)' suffix; that was added in the entry.

claims_in_notes_disputed: ENOTO is described as using 'progressive relaxation of the ensemble target' (in the notes under (b) and in the ENOTO summary: 'progressively relaxes... moving from min-style to mean or weighted targets'). Per Algorithm 1 of arXiv v4 (IJCAI 2024), ENOTO switches once at the start of online fine-tuning from a MinQ target to a WeightedMinPair target (the expectation of pairwise-min targets) and adds SUNRISE-style ensemble exploration. The paper describes no progressive or annealed schedule. A gradual, per-action relaxation would therefore differ somewhat more from ENOTO than the notes imply.

The PBRL summary says 'The paper also includes an offline-to-online experiment with a decaying penalty.' No such experiment exists: a full-text search of arXiv 2202.11566 finds no fine-tuning or offline-to-online section. The decay is of the OOD penalty weight beta_ood during offline training (5.0 to 0.2, linear for 50K steps then exponential). PBRL is offline-only.

CCVF is described as adapting 'one global confidence level from returns observed online'. The paper's confidence-adaptive policy picks delta from the observation history using a Bellman-consistency criterion (Sec. 4.2, after Ghosh et al. 2022), not from returns. The notes also leave out that CCVF already includes an online fine-tuning experiment on 5 Atari games (Sec. 7.3), so it is discrete-action O2O prior art for adaptive conservatism.

The notes treat the Rezaeifar et al. AAAI venue and the ENOTO IJCAI venue as unconfirmed. Both are now confirmed: AAAI 2022 (Proc. AAAI 36(7):8106-8114, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v36i7.20783) and IJCAI 2024 (pp. 5563-5571, DOI 10.24963/ijcai.2024/615).

A minor imprecision about SUNG ('top-p% hard gating'): SUNG marks the top p% of each minibatch by uncertainty as OOD with a binary identifier, but the paper says the selection 'can be performed by sampling from a categorical distribution', so it may be stochastic rather than a deterministic hard top-p%. The contrast with our 'soft continuous weighting' still holds (binary versus continuous weight), but it should be stated as binary identifier versus continuous weight. On AntMaze, SUNG uses SPOT rather than TD3+BC as the conservative objective.

A minor imprecision about MOPO ('ensemble max std'): the MOPO penalty is the maximum, over ensemble members, of the norm of each probabilistic model's predicted std (aleatoric), not the disagreement across members.
topic_notes:
Bottom line: every one of options (a)-(d) has close prior art, mostly in continuous control (D4RL). None is new as an algorithm. What is new is the setting: discrete-action recommendation where the behavior policy is known, plus ablations that use oracle support, which D4RL cannot provide.

(a) Support- or density-weighted conservatism. Closest prior work:
- SUNG (Guo et al., arXiv 2023; IEEE TNNLS 2025): a VAE density model, updated online, sets a binary OOD identifier on the top-p% most uncertain samples of each minibatch (possibly selected by categorical sampling). Those samples get the conservative objective (CQL, TD3+BC, or SPOT on AntMaze) during fine-tuning.
- SPOT (NeurIPS 2022): a VAE log pi_beta regularizer. During fine-tuning, lambda decays linearly and stops at 20% at step 0.8M, and the VAE stays frozen.
- SVR (NeurIPS 2023): penalizes Q over the whole OOD set using importance sampling with pi_beta.
- Count-MORL: count-based penalties.
- ACL-QL: learned per-(s,a) CQL weights.
- DORL (SIGIR 2023): on KuaiRec, pessimism is relaxed by logging-policy entropy (offline, model-based).
- DARE (arXiv 2025-26): sample-level, hard, balanced constraint relaxation during O2O, driven by deviation from a diffusion behavior model's reference action.

What would remain ours:
- exact and oracle pi_beta(a|s) over 500-3000 discrete items;
- soft, continuous weighting inside a discrete CQL or SVR penalty instead of a binary top-p% identifier;
- recommendation-specific outcomes (long-tail exposure, coverage).

These are differences of instantiation and analysis, not of idea.

(b) Critic-ensemble disagreement. Closest prior work:
- Offline: PBRL (offline-only; it has no O2O experiment), EDAC/SAC-N, UWAC (dropout).
- During fine-tuning: Lee et al. (pessimistic Q-ensemble plus balanced replay); ENOTO (IJCAI 2024), which switches once from a MinQ to a WeightedMinPair target at the start of online fine-tuning and adds SUNRISE-style ensemble exploration; Neggatu et al. (uncertainty-based switching, extends to O2O).

A gradual or per-action relaxation would extend ENOTO's one-time switch. What would remain ours: a direct test of whether ensemble disagreement tracks the true logging support, for example AUROC of disagreement for detecting items with pi_beta < epsilon. PBRL's linear-MDP theory (ensemble std approximates the elliptical LCB term) says it should, and our simulator can check this.

(c) Restricting policy shift on low-support actions. Closest prior work:
- Discrete BCQ: the threshold G(a|s)/max G > tau is exactly a support mask over discrete actions.
- BEAR's support (MMD) constraint.
- SPOT; FamO2O (state-adaptive constraint strength); adaptive BC weighting (Zhao et al.).
- CCVF (ICLR 2023): a confidence-conditioned Q; at evaluation time it picks delta from the history via Bellman consistency. It is discrete-action and includes Atari online fine-tuning.

What would remain ours: an item-level trust region during fine-tuning, for example KL(pi || pi_offline) weighted by 1/support, or a tau that relaxes as online counts for an item accumulate. This is close to "discrete BCQ with an online-count-updated mask".

(d) Dynamic offline/online replay mixing. Closest prior work:
- Balanced replay (density-ratio prioritization), RLPD (50/50 sampling, LayerNorm, a 10-critic ensemble), APL (pessimistic on offline samples, optimistic on online ones), WSRL (offline data can be dropped after a warm-up), Cal-QL.

This option has the weakest novelty, and RLPD and WSRL are strong controls for it.

Recommendation: present (a) as a design study, "Does the support signal matter for conservatism during fine-tuning in discrete recommendation?", with (b) and RND or counts as alternative estimators of the same quantity. Its key advantage is testability: the simulator knows the true pi_beta and the true Q, so it can separate "the support signal helps" from "any adaptivity helps" and from "less conservatism helps". Claim the instantiation and the analysis, not a new algorithm. Cite SUNG, SPOT, SVR, DARE and DORL as the direct antecedents, and CCVF as discrete-action O2O adaptive-conservatism prior art.

Required ablations:
